title: Pacific approach — off the Farallon Islands
short_location: US Pacific EEZ, west of San Francisco, California

gallery.blurb: Different ocean, different year, same pipeline. Does the method hold?

notes: Second basin — the case that proves case 1 was not a fluke, and the hero backup if offshore AIS coverage fails at Jacksonville. Target acts: detect, trace, attribute, verify. Export box -124.0113 37.7094 -123.8013 37.8895, 82% inside the scene footprint (the footprint edge cuts the east side; shifting east made it worse, so the box is tightened instead), dB clamp [-28, -14]. cerulean_slick.geojson is Cerulean slick 3687325 (19.63 km, 3.85 km2, model confidence 0.929) — comparison target, not ground truth. CARE: this Sentinel-1 scene carries at least four separate Cerulean slicks, including two much larger ones (126 km and 76 km) and another on the adjacent 14:24:17 frame. Ours is the 19.6 km feature. If Stage 1 returns a detection an order of magnitude larger, it has found a different slick, not a better one — check the geometry before assuming a segmentation bug.
